sources.readScope: 29.1.1 early-z and bounding-volume occlusion query explanation
sources.use: Distinguish fragment depth rejection from object-level conservative occlusion. A query bounding box is not an occluder to write into the depth buffer.
Explicit depth extrema and conservative approximations. Collision-testing example is not treated as the Hi-Z algorithm.
Frustum and occlusion distinction, conservative AABB queries and keeping partially visible objects. CPU sample performance is not generalized.
CPU-specific masked method and separation of rasterization/query. Linked paper PDF fetch failed; no full-paper read claimed.

sources.readScope: Returned lines0–394, coarse shading, tiers, full coverage/depth, interpolation and derivative caveats
sources.use: Separate shading frequency from output pixel count. A2×2 evaluation diagram is independent and not a fourfold measured speedup.
Mesh/amplification geometry workgroups and primitive outputs, not indirect-light computation.
Feedback reports desired texture regions/mips. Requested pages and resident data are different states; streaming need not use feedback.

independentMathExample.scope: Original4×4 depth grid and2×2 reduction, not reconstruction of a named engine implementation.
independentMathExample.standardDepth: Near0/far1: max reduction over every covered sample; reject only when conservative nearest candidate depth exceeds the farthest occluder throughout the covered footprint.
independentMathExample.reverseDepth: Near1/far0: min reduction and comparison direction reverse together.
independentMathExample.coverage: Clear/uncovered samples carry far depth, preventing false rejection; conservative bounds/footprint coverage/precision remain required.
independentMathExample.temporal: Earlier depth alone does not establish current occlusion after camera or occluder motion. The original animation illustrates this risk without claiming one universal engine fix.
